conflicts: 4s 3S°1 lifetime: beam-foil 1.875(0.094) ns (Beideck et al. 1994, kept) vs 1.5(0.3) ns (Savage & Lawrence 1966) and 1.4 ns (Mueller 1968); B-spline R-matrix theory 1.93 ns supports the beam-foil value.
3P0 - 4s 3S°1 (182.62 nm): Beideck's measured branching fraction 0.069(13) gives A = 3.7(7)e7 s^-1, whereas NIST ASD lists 5.64e7 s^-1 (LS-like ratio); the two stronger lines agree with NIST.

5p 5P3 lifetime: 615(50) ns (Delalic et al. 1990) vs '<97(30)' ns (Bridges & Wiese 1968) vs theory 130-165 ns (HFR, Opacity Project, B-spline R-matrix 158 ns). The Delalic value is kept as the only direct lifetime measurement but looks inconsistent with every calculation.
3d 3D° lifetime: 2.1(0.3) ns (Savage & Lawrence, multiplet) vs 3.0(0.6) ns (Federman & Cardelli, astronomical) vs 3.7 ns (B-spline R-matrix) vs '<1.5' ns (Mueller).

4d 3D°, 5s-8s 3S°, 5d, 6d 3D°: the laser lifetimes are about twice the relativistic Hartree-Fock values of the same authors (e.g. 4d 3D° 12.6 vs 6.0 ns; 6d 3D° 75(7) vs 16 ns); for 6d 3D° and 8s 3S° the astronomical values (199(90), 73(44) ns) are longer still.
4s'' 3P° lifetime: beam-foil 2.034(0.102) / 2.146(0.129) ns (kept) vs phase shift 2.8(0.3) ns (Smith 1978) vs '<1.2' ns (Mueller 1968).
3d 1P°1 (81438 cm^-1): 17(2) ns measured by Savage & Lawrence for the level they call 3s3p5 1P1 at 81440.3 cm^-1; B-spline R-matrix 13.9 ns.
4p 3P lifetime: 46.1(1.0) ns (Zerne et al. 1997, kept) vs 33(12) ns (Bridges & Wiese arc) vs HFR 36 ns; B-spline R-matrix 46.3 ns agrees with the laser value.

Level energies of 4p 3P: Lai et al. 2020 find the older compilation (Martin, Zalubas, Musgrove 1990) too high by 0.032 cm^-1 for all three levels; the current NIST values (64888.9325, 64891.3536, 64892.5514) already include the correction.
not_found: 33S hyperfine structure of the 3p4 3P ground term or of any excited level: no measurement exists according to Carette & Godefroid 2011; only their calculated A and B are given
measured lifetime of the metastable 4s 5S°2 level (N. J. Mason, Phys. Scr. 49, 578 (1994)): paper not accessible; theory value given

measured absolute A-values of the forbidden lines 458.9 nm (1S0-3P1) and 772.5 nm (1S0-1D2) (Kernahan & Pang, Can. J. Phys. 53, 1114 (1975)): only the first sentence of the abstract could be opened, no numbers; measured lifetimes of 1D2 and 1S0 not located

original tables of Berzinsh et al., Phys. Rev. A 55, 1836 (1997), Zerne et al., Phys. Scr. 56, 459 (1997), Li et al., Eur. Phys. J. D 2, 11 (1998) and Delalic et al., Phys. Scr. 42, 540 (1990): paywalled; values taken from the Biemont et al. 1998 comparison table and from the Zerne abstract
lifetimes of 4p 5P1,2,3, 4s' 3D°1,2,3, 3d 5D°1,2,3, 5p 5P1,2, 4s'' 1P°1: no measurement located, B-spline R-matrix values given and marked theory

lifetimes of 3s3p5 3P°2,1 (72023.471, 72382.305 cm^-1), 5d 3D°2 (78691.43 cm^-1; only J=1 and J=3 are listed), 12d 3D°3 (82723.25 cm^-1): nothing usable (the B-spline R-matrix table gives 6.5-6.7 microseconds for 3s3p5 3P°, which disagrees with the NIST A-values by a factor of about 7, so it is not included)
33S and 36S isotope shifts; isotope shifts of any one-photon line: none located (only 34S-32S on the 3P2 - 4p 3P2 two-photon line)

laser cooling: no scheme for atomic sulfur located

notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/S_I_levels.tsv). Uncertainties copied from Biemont et al. 1998 Table 1 are 2 sigma ('b represents a 2 sigma uncertainty'); Beideck et al. 1994 uncertainties are 1 sigma as printed in the original (Biemont et al. list them doubled). Lifetimes attributed to Berzinsh et al. 1997, Delalic et al. 1990, Bridges & Wiese, Smith 1978, Mueller 1968, Federman & Cardelli 1995 are second-hand (method 'compilation'). The Federman & Cardelli 'lifetimes' are inferred from interstellar absorption f-values, not laboratory lifetimes. Savage & Lawrence values are multiplet lifetimes attached to each fine-structure level. A-values of the 3P - ns 3S°, nd 3D° lines from Biemont et al. are semi-empirical (measured lifetime x calculated branching ratio); they are close to what NIST ASD already lists. 'f_abs' (absorption oscillator strength) is a non-schema field; type 'two-photon' is used for the Doppler-free two-photon lines (frequency = total energy of both photons). 32S and 34S have I = 0; 33S has I = 3/2. Lifetimes of 1D2 and 1S0 are derived from calculated A-values (theory).
